name: _sparse_bsc_tensor_unsafe
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_sparse_bsc_tensor_unsafe(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. This is the only supplied registered schema string: aten::_sparse_bsc_tensor_unsafe(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. The original Gems pytest (tests/test__sparse_bsc_tensor_unsafe.py) owns the full contract: positional and keyword call forms, omitted optional keywords (dtype/layout fall back to defaults, pin_memory), the error cases (missing size, non-tensor pointer, negative extent, dtype mismatch, wrong layout, device mismatch, accelerator payload with pin_memory), storage aliasing/mutation visibility (with the pinned-copy case noted below), component metadata preservation (stride, storage offset, stride pattern), index dtypes int64/int32, empty and rank<2 sizes, dense tails, special values and autograd-inert behavior; never narrow or remove those tests to fit this one signature. Semantics: a host-side factory that installs ccol_indices, row_indices and values into a sparse-BSC TensorImpl without validating or densifying the descriptor contents (pointer/row lengths and index bounds are unchecked); it does reject invalid arguments such as a negative extent, a dtype that does not match the values dtype, a non-BSC layout, a device mismatch, or pin_memory with an accelerator payload. It stores the requested size verbatim and adopts the requested dtype, which must equal the values dtype; when dtype is omitted the global default dtype applies and the values must match it. For the ordinary unpinned construction it keeps each component tensor's own dtype, shape, stride and storage offset, and aliases the component storages so writes through the input tensors or through the returned sparse tensor's components are mutually visible; with pin_memory=True on a dense CPU payload the components are instead copied into pinned storage and no storage is shared with the inputs. The returned tensor is a new object (not a plain view of any single parameter), so no output-to-parameter alias is modelled here even though its components alias the given tensors in the unpinned case; effects are recorded for this representative overload only and conditional behavior is defined by the pytest. Note: the supplied type hints render ATen's non-JSON optional keyword types as Optional[int] for the dtype/layout enums (ScalarType?/Layout?), Optional[Device] for device and Optional[bool] for pin_memory, with JSON null defaults; these stable renderings are retained as given rather than replaced with guessed Python objects.
